best_human.source_location: Varshamov and Tenengolts (1965) introduce the checksum class; Levenshtein establishes single-deletion correction; 2026 paper §2.2 states the code definition.
best_human.provenance: Reconstructed directly from VT_0(16): sum(i*x_i) is 0 modulo 17.
best_human.ai_provenance: Classical human construction; no generative-AI provenance.
best_human.evidence_state: The exact checker confirms no two codewords share any one-deletion output.

best_public.provenance: Table records the classical VT_0(16) code size as 3856. This is a feasible-code record, not a claim that 3856 is the maximum.
best_public.ai_provenance: Classical construction; source separately reports an AI-assisted rediscovery with the same size.
best_public.evidence_state: The locally frozen code and exact deletion-output check reproduce the size.

best_reproduced.provenance: Frozen VT_0(16) list independently compared with the checksum formula and fully verified.
best_reproduced.ai_provenance: The 2026 paper reports an AI-assisted priority-function rediscovery equivalent to VT_0; this task's witness is generated from the classical formula.
best_reproduced.evidence_state: Exact pairwise check over all distinct deletion outputs.

ai_assisted_record.provenance: LLM-guided evolutionary search rediscovered a priority function proved to generate VT_0; same cardinality as the classical code.
ai_assisted_record.evidence_state: Reported by source; separately identified as AI-assisted and not a larger code or an optimality proof.

highest_reported.metric: codewords in a binary length-16 one-deletion-correcting code
highest_reported.reproduction_status: The reported feasible construction is reproduced exactly. The source gives an LP upper bound of 4202, so the finite maximum is not settled.

optimality_status.state: open; the paper says the VT maximum-size conjecture is proved only for lengths up to 11
